pointers.sentence: How a feed, a subclass of `django.contrib.syndication.views.Feed`, answers a request with an RSS or Atom document: the object it is about, the attributes that may each be a value or a method, and the feed generator of `django/utils/feedgenerator.py`, a `SyndicationFeed` such as `Rss201rev2Feed` or `Atom1Feed`, which writes the XML.
The view knows the request: it finds the object, takes the current site's domain for links, renders templates and makes dates aware (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed`).
The **feed generator** knows nothing of requests or models: it keeps what it is handed in dictionaries and writes one dialect of XML (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:SyndicationFeed`).

The URLconf holds one instance of a `Feed` subclass (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed`), and every request to its pattern calls that one object ([What the handler asks of a view](../views/callable.md)).
`Feed.__call__` does four things (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.__call__`):

It makes an `HttpResponse` with the generator's `content_type`, and, if the feed has an attribute `"item_pubdate"` or `"item_updateddate"`, a Last-Modified header from `SyndicationFeed.latest_post_date`, the newest date of any item or else the present, so that, says the comment, `ConditionalGetMiddleware` can answer 304 ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md#conditionalgetmiddleware)).

Every part of a feed but four plain attributes, `Feed.feed_type`, `Feed.language`, `Feed.title_template` and `Feed.description_template`, and two methods always called, `Feed.feed_extra_kwargs` and `Feed.item_extra_kwargs`, is read through `Feed._get_dynamic_attr`, with one argument: the object from `Feed.get_object` for a part of the feed, the item for a part of an item (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed._get_dynamic_attr`).
`Feed.get_feed` works in this order (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.get_feed`):

The feed's link, its `"feed_url"` and each item's link go through `add_domain`: a path gets the scheme, `"https"` when `HttpRequest.is_secure` says so, and the domain; a URL beginning `"http://"`, `"https://"` or `"mailto:"` is left alone, and one beginning `"//"` gets the scheme, which RSS requires, says the comment, citing ticket 16753 (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:add_domain`).

An enclosure's URL is no link: `Feed.item_enclosures` makes at most one `Enclosure`, from `"item_enclosure_url"`, `"item_enclosure_length"` and `"item_enclosure_mime_type"`, each through `str`, so a missing length is written `"None"` (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.item_enclosures`).

`Feed.item_title` escapes the item's `str` as HTML, and its comment says titles should be double escaped by default, citing ticket 6533 (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.item_title`); the generator escapes again, as XML.

`SyndicationFeed.__init__` keeps the feed's values in a dictionary, text made strings and URLs escaped, the id `"feed_guid"` or else the link, and any keyword it does not know (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:SyndicationFeed.__init__`); `SyndicationFeed.add_item` appends one for each item.

`RssFeed.write` makes a `SimplerXMLGenerator` over the file ([Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md#the-xml-writer)) and writes the declaration, any stylesheets, an rss element and a channel, the feed's elements and the items (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:RssFeed.write`); `Atom1Feed.write`, a feed element and entries.

`RssFeed.write` makes a `SimplerXMLGenerator` over the file ([Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md#the-xml-writer)) and writes the declaration, any stylesheets, an rss element and a channel, the feed's elements and the items (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:RssFeed.write`); `Atom1Feed.write`, a feed element and entries.
A format built on RSS or Atom subclasses `Rss201rev2Feed` or `Atom1Feed` and extends them, calling the superclass's, says the documentation (`docs/ref/contrib/syndication.txt`).

GeoDjango's `Feed` uses one, `GeoRSSFeed`, handing it geometries through its own `feed_extra_kwargs` and `item_extra_kwargs` (`django/contrib/gis/feeds.py:Feed`) ([GeoDjango's forms, admin, feeds and data tools](gis-extras.md)).
*The generators of `django/utils/feedgenerator.py`.

An Atom entry with no unique id gets one from `get_tag_uri`; from a feed view, only when `"item_guid"` returns `None`, as in `"tag:harbour.example,2026-10-13:/bulletins/2//"` (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:get_tag_uri`).
The feed generators take stylesheets (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

Each is a URL, made a `Stylesheet`, or a `Stylesheet`, whose type is guessed from the extension unless given, whose media is `"screen"` unless given, and whose URL is read only when written, so a lazy one from `reverse_lazy` works (`django/utils/feedgenerator.py:Stylesheet`).
